name: Segmentation
description: Divide an object/system into independent parts; make it easy to assemble/disassemble; increase the degree of fragmentation.

name: Taking out (extraction)
description: Separate an interfering part or property from an object, or extract the one necessary part/property.

name: Local quality
description: Change a uniform structure/property into a non-uniform one; make each part suited to its own local function.

name: Asymmetry
description: Replace a symmetrical form with an asymmetrical one; if already asymmetrical, increase the asymmetry.

name: Merging (consolidation)
description: Bring closer together, or merge, identical or related objects/operations so they run in parallel or as one.

name: Universality
description: Make one part or object perform multiple functions, eliminating the need for other parts.

name: Nesting
description: Place one object inside another; that inside a third; and so on ("Russian doll").

name: Anti-weight (counterweight)
description: Compensate for an object's weight by merging it with objects that provide lift, or by interaction with the environment (aerodynamic, hydrodynamic, buoyant forces).

name: Preliminary anti-action
description: If an action will have both harmful and useful effects, perform an anti-action in advance to control the harmful effect.

name: Preliminary action
description: Perform the required change of an object, in full or in part, before it is needed.

name: Beforehand cushioning (compensation)
description: Prepare emergency backup/compensation means in advance to offset the relatively low reliability of an object.

name: Equipotentiality
description: Change operating conditions so an object doesn't need to be raised or lowered (eliminate potential-energy transitions).

name: The other way round (inversion)
description: Invert the action; make movable parts fixed and fixed parts movable; turn the object/process upside down.

name: Spheroidality / curvature
description: Replace flat surfaces/straight lines/cubic forms with curved, spherical, or rounded ones; use rollers, balls, spirals.

name: Dynamics
description: Allow (or design in) characteristics, an object, or a process to change to be optimal at each stage of operation; divide into parts capable of movement relative to each other.

name: Partial or excessive action
description: If 100% of an effect is hard to achieve directly, use slightly less or slightly more to simplify the problem.

name: Another dimension
description: Move an object/process into two or three dimensions instead of one; use a multi-story arrangement; tilt or reorient it.

name: Mechanical vibration
description: Cause an object to oscillate or vibrate; increase frequency (even to ultrasonic); use resonance.

name: Periodic action
description: Replace a continuous action with a periodic or pulsed one; if already periodic, change the frequency or pattern.

name: Continuity of useful action
description: Carry out work continuously, with all parts of a system operating at full load, eliminating idle/intermediate motion.

name: Skipping (rushing through)
description: Conduct a process, or particularly its harmful/hazardous stages, at high speed.

name: Blessing in disguise (convert harm to benefit)
description: Use harmful factors/effects to achieve a positive outcome, or eliminate a harmful factor by combining it with another harmful factor.

name: Feedback
description: Introduce feedback to monitor and improve a process; if feedback already exists, change its magnitude or timing.

name: Intermediary
description: Use an intermediary object/process to carry out an action, or temporarily merge one object with another that's easily removed.

name: Self-service
description: Make an object serve itself by performing auxiliary, repair, or maintenance functions; make use of waste resources.

name: Copying
description: Use a simple, cheap copy (optical, digital, simulated) instead of an object that is complex, expensive, fragile, or inconvenient to use directly.

name: Cheap short-living objects
description: Replace an expensive object with multiple cheap ones, trading off qualities like longevity for cost.

name: Mechanics substitution
description: Replace a mechanical means with a sensory one (optical, acoustic, thermal, olfactory); use fields to interact with the object instead.

name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
description: Replace solid parts of an object with gas or liquid; use air/water cushions, inflatable, or hydrostatic elements.

name: Flexible shells and thin films
description: Replace conventional/rigid structures with flexible shells or thin films; isolate an object using thin flexible membranes.

name: Porous materials
description: Make an object porous or add porous elements; if already porous, fill the pores in advance with something useful.

name: Color / optical property changes
description: Change the color or transparency of an object or its surroundings to change its perceived or actual properties.

name: Homogeneity
description: Make objects that interact with a given object out of the same (or property-matched) material.

name: Discarding and recovering
description: Make parts that have finished their function disappear (dissolve, degrade, self-eject) or be restored during operation.

name: Parameter changes
description: Change an object's physical/chemical state, concentration, consistency, flexibility, or temperature.

name: Phase transitions
description: Use phenomena occurring during a phase transition (volume change, heat absorption/release, etc.).

name: Thermal expansion
description: Use thermal expansion or contraction of a material; combine materials with different expansion coefficients.

name: Strong oxidants (accelerated oxidation)
description: Replace normal air/environment with an enriched, ionized, or accelerated-reaction one to speed a process.

name: Inert atmosphere
description: Replace a normal environment with an inert one; carry out a process in vacuum.

name: Composite materials
description: Replace a homogeneous material with a composite one, combining materials to get properties neither has alone.
